thesis: Accenture's FY2026 Q4 earnings (reported 2026-10-01, fiscal year ended Aug 31) beat estimates across the board -- revenue $18.68B (+6%) above the high end of guidance, GAAP EPS $3.29 vs ~$3.18 consensus, and FY2027 guidance raised to 3-6% local-currency revenue growth with GAAP EPS of $14.39-$14.81 -- driving a record one-day ~16% share surge on 5.6x average volume. This supports a long entry even though managed-services new bookings fell ~15% sequentially to $9.1B, since management attributed the drop to large deals pushed from Q3 into FY2027 for company-specific timing reasons rather than demand erosion, pointing to Q4's managed-services strength coming from newly closed deals and core consulting bookings up 13% YoY as evidence the underlying pipeline remains intact.
invalidation: A confirmed demand slowdown showing up in FY2027 managed-services bookings, a guidance walk-back, or a concrete adverse development in the open securities-fraud investigations tied to the June 2026 guidance cut would invalidate this.

thesis: Cenovus saw an elevated-volume session (14.93M shares vs a 6.47M 30-day average, ~2.3x) amid a sector-wide energy-stock rotation (TSX energy names outperforming) layered on a company-specific analyst re-rating -- National Bank Financial set a Street-high C$60 target (Outperform) on Sept 30, and JPMorgan upgraded to Overweight on Sept 3 -- alongside falling net debt (down to $5.4B) and an active buyback. This is offset by UBS's late-August downgrade to Hold on valuation grounds and multiple screens flagging the stock as overvalued after its run to a Sept 15 all-time high, so the evidence here reads as mixed rather than a clean directional signal, and part of today's move is sector rotation rather than purely company-specific.
invalidation: A reversal of the energy-sector rotation, a pullback in National Bank's valuation case, or a shift to an operationally negative catalyst (e.g. a stalled Deep Basin asset sale or a weak Q3 print) would invalidate this; a confirmed resolution of the valuation debate in bulls' favor would strengthen it.

thesis: Coherent jumped ~11% today on Bernstein's new Outperform initiation ($350 target) framing optical/photonics suppliers as structural AI-datacenter winners, with peers Lumentum (+9%) and Corning (+3%) rallying in sympathy -- a sector-sentiment and analyst-initiation event rather than new company-disclosed operating data. The move doesn't resolve the bear case that drove COHR down ~28% from its June 52-week high: co-packaged-optics (PhotonLink) revenue is still guided to begin ramping only in late CY2026 with meaningful contribution in 2027, and the stock remains priced for a smooth ramp with little room for slippage.
invalidation: Confirmation of a CPO/PhotonLink ramp delay or margin miss at the Nov 11, 2026 fiscal Q1 earnings report, or an escalation of the open 2025-origin securities-fraud investigations or BIS/Huawei inquiry, would invalidate this; continued customer LTA announcements or an on-schedule ramp would strengthen it.

thesis: ArcelorMittal fell ~3.3% today (and is down ~10% over 60 days) amid a broad metals/materials-sector selloff -- coal, aluminum, rare earths and European steel all declined together on Sep 30-Oct 1 while the S&P 500 rose -- rather than any MT-specific negative news; the company separately idled part of its Gijon, Spain long-products line due to soft wire-rod demand. This still supports a long read even though the triggering move is sector-wide, because the EU's anti-circumvention 'melt and pour' rule became mandatory Oct 1 (closing a China-origin rerolling loophole), Eurozone manufacturing PMI hit a post-2022 high in September, and ArcelorMittal just raised European HRC prices EUR20/t for November delivery -- none of which point to the deteriorating demand the price action implies.
invalidation: A confirmed company-specific negative (an earnings miss, a stalled asset sale, an adverse Milan lawsuit development) or a failure of the EU melt-and-pour rule to curb China-origin volumes would invalidate this; continued pricing power and PMI improvement would strengthen it.

thesis: ASML's bull case remains intact with no material new developments since yesterday: FY2026 revenue guidance stays raised to EUR43-45B on AI-driven fab capex, and analyst sentiment stays net-constructive (Cantor Overweight, Jefferies Neutral, UBS Buy with a EUR2,350 target ahead of earnings) even as Morgan Stanley trimmed its target to EUR1,700 and Weiss downgraded to Hold on China/margin risk. This still supports holding even though the open, unresolved US Commerce Dept probe into an alleged China EUV shipment breach (ASML denies it) remains outstanding with no scheduled ruling date, because the Oct 14, 2026 Q3 earnings report -- a real pending binary catalyst just 13 days out -- could still move the read before the next cycle.
invalidation: A confirmed export-control violation finding, a guidance walk-back or demand slowdown at the Oct 14 print, or an escalation of the Commerce Dept probe to a formal enforcement action would invalidate this.

thesis: TMO's bull case stays supported: Thermo Fisher's 3.3% pullback today to ~$652 reads as valuation digestion after its run to a fresh 52-week high ($683.63 on Sep 24), not a new negative catalyst -- GuruFocus flags the stock ~8.5% above fair value, but analyst upgrades continued into late September (Deutsche Bank to $720, UBS to Buy at $730, HSBC Strong Buy) on the same 5-6% 2027 organic-growth and margin-expansion (22.8% vs 21.9%) thesis as before. This still supports holding even though an antibody-catalog data-integrity controversy and a surviving single-plaintiff Title VII claim (Deans v. Thermo Fisher) remain open, because neither has triggered a formal regulatory investigation or a scheduled near-term ruling, and the next real test -- the Oct 21, 2026 Q3 earnings/guidance print -- is still 3 weeks out.
invalidation: A guidance cut or an organic-growth miss versus the 5-6% 2027 target at the Oct 21 print, a formal regulatory probe opening into the antibody-data allegations, or a reversal of the recent analyst upgrades would invalidate this.
sources: CourtListener (Deans v. Thermo Fisher, surviving Title VII claim): https://www.courtlistener.com/opinion/10873491/greta-deans-v-thermo-fisher-scientific-inc/

thesis: Lumentum jumped further today (~$1046 vs ~$971 prior close) on Bernstein's new Outperform initiation ($1,220 target) and reports that the Trump administration/FCC is drafting a rule banning new Chinese-made optical transceivers in AI datacenters, which, if finalized, could redirect share to Lumentum -- but that rule remains an unconfirmed draft that 'could be modified, delayed or abandoned,' not a locked-in catalyst, layered on top of an already-stretched valuation from the NVIDIA-backed AI-optics buildout. This is offset by the stock now trading at roughly 142x trailing earnings versus a 5-year median near 42x, GF Value flagging ~489% overvaluation, and 12 months of insider selling with zero insider buying -- real counter-evidence that the position is now priced for a regulatory outcome that hasn't happened yet, even though nothing in the underlying AI-optics demand story has broken down.
invalidation: A delay or abandonment of the reported Chinese-transceiver import rule, a slowdown in AI-datacenter optics orders, or an adverse outcome in the open BIS/DOJ export-control inquiry would invalidate this; confirmation of the rule as final, or a beat-and-raise quarter validating the current multiple, would strengthen it.

thesis: Carvana's operating momentum stays intact -- Oppenheimer raised its target to $90 on Sept 30 citing September unit sales running well above Street estimates, and the company closed a $1.66B Term Loan B on Sept 23 extending debt maturities to 2033, continuing its balance-sheet repair (S&P 500 inclusion, early 2026). This doesn't resolve the credibility overhang from the January 2026 Gotham City Research report alleging $1B+ of undisclosed related-party dealings with Garcia-family-controlled DriveTime/Bridgecrest/GoFi: those securities-fraud claims remain unresolved with active multi-firm investigations, even though the core securities class action's dispositive-motions date was reset to Jan 25, 2027 (beyond the near-term window) rather than the Nov 4, 2026 date previously tracked, so the evidence here stays mixed rather than a clean read.
invalidation: An adverse ruling, an SEC enforcement action, or expanded related-party findings in the ongoing litigation/investigations would invalidate this hold; a dismissal of the securities claims or continued unit-growth beats into the Oct 28, 2026 earnings report would strengthen it.
sources: CourtListener docket (securities litigation, dispositive motions reset to 1/25/2027): https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/66654699/in-re-carvana-co-securities-litigation/
